editorial: Cadence is becoming the defining signal this week. SUMERIAN shows what sustained content flow looks like. Across the roster, the channels that go quiet between releases see momentum soften quickly — even lightweight follow-through keeps recommendation signals active.
insights: Audience growth remains the clearest opportunity across the roster. Tom Odell and James Blake are pulling discovery, but the channels converting best this week are pairing Shorts with deeper formats — BTS, live clips, artist-led context.

Cadence is becoming a defining signal. JJerome87 and Lykke Li both show how quickly momentum softens between releases when channels go quiet. Even lightweight follow-through — catalogue Shorts, archive clips, reactions — helps keep recommendation signals active.

The strongest campaign ecosystems this week came from TEN, Jutes, SAINT CLAIR. Consistent uploads beyond release day — Shorts, longform and supporting formats working together — continue to outperform single-drop strategies.

The clearest roster-wide pattern remains the 7–10 day follow-through window. Campaigns extending momentum are continuing the story after release day — BTS, reaction clips, a Shorts remix — rather than treating the official video as the endpoint.

playbook.title: Release Day Content Stack
playbook.why: The first 72 hours determine algorithmic trajectory. YouTube recommends multiple content touchpoints on release day.
playbook.when: Release week for any single, album, or major video.
actions: Day 0: Official video + announcement Short + Community Post
Day 1–2: BTS or making-of showing the creative process
Day 3–5: Lyric video or visualiser for a second content surface
